Cayo is  probably the number one stop for travelers looking to spend a few days in Belize’s mainland.

Known as the cultural heart of Belize, Cayo presents a wealth of natural attractions, concentration of Mayan sites, and an excellent display of local cuisine. It’s also just a short 30-mile drive to Corozal Town. The entrance to Orange Walk is marked by the country’s sole tollbooth, where a modest fee of about US 50 cents is collected. As you pass through, two prominent features immediately capture your attention: the picturesque New River, lined with tour guide operators, and the towering smokestacks of the former sugar mill. While sugar once dominated the town, its influence has waned, leaving a new era for Orange Walk to embrace.

en.h1: Tours to Resort Placencia in Belize
en.title: Placencia resort in Belize in the Caribbean Tours & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Belize  with Ada Tours
content_excerpts: Placencia resort in Belize in the Caribbean Tours & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Belize  with Ada Tours

Placencia, a stunning emerald peninsula in southern Belize, boasts 16 miles of pristine sandy beaches. To the east lies the sparkling Caribbean Sea, while the serene Placencia Lagoon to the west is framed by the majestic mountains of the mainland. The peninsula is naturally divided into two sections: the area south of the airstrip and the area north of it. Exploring Placencia is a breeze with a beach cruiser bike, allowing you to easily navigate this picturesque locale. The southern part of Placencia is the bustling hub, home to a vibrant mix of coffee shops, bistros, internet cafes, the harbor, guesthouses, and essential services like taxi and bus stations, banks, and local eateries.

The northern section of Placencia, which encompasses the Garifuna village of Seine Bight, is more sparsely populated and features several upscale resorts. Situated farther from the reef, this area experiences genuine, albeit modest, surf. The waters here are crystal clear, with gentle trade winds providing a refreshing breeze. Few experiences are as tranquil as watching a Belizean sunset from a secluded beach on the Placencia Peninsula, offering a serene and soul-soothing escape.

en.title: Punta Gorda Tours & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Belize  with Ada Tours
content_excerpts: Nestled on the western shores of the Caribbean Sea, Punta Gorda Town graces the southern expanse of Belize, where it serves as the gateway to the Gulf of Honduras. This coastal town is more than just a picturesque locale; it stands as the administrative heart of the Toledo District, a region rich in cultural heritage and natural beauty.

Punta Gorda is your portal to the wonders of the Toledo District, where adventure meets history at every turn. Whether you're casting a line in the turquoise waters offshore, navigating serene rivers, exploring hidden caves, or marveling at the vibrant birdlife, Punta Gorda offers an unparalleled introduction to Belize’s treasures. The district's rich tapestry of Maya archaeological sites and natural wonders ensures that every traveler finds something extraordinary to discover.

The city in Amatique Bay on the Caribbean coast is ideal for both passive and active recreation. A number of sandy beaches stretch along the city coastline. There is a market on the main street of Punta Gorda, where you can feel not only the local flavor, but also the whole of Belize, buy handmade products from different parts of the country.

To top it all off, Toledo is a district not only filled with natural beauty in abundance but also home to some of the nicest people. Here Maya, Garifuna and East Indian Belizeans live harmoniously while maintaining their individual cultures.

content_excerpts: Tours to Copacabana & Lake Titicaca(Bolivia)   & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Bolivia  with Ada Tours

Embark on an unforgettable trip to Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, with one of our expertly crafted Bolivia tours. Whether you're seeking a guided tour to Lake Titicaca or planning to explore on your own, our travel packages are designed to showcase the best of this stunning region.

Choose a tour to Lake Titicaca that fits your interests, from exploring the floating islands of the Uros people to discovering the rich cultural heritage of the region. Our Bolivia travel packages offer a seamless experience, ensuring that your journey is both enriching and hassle-free.

Whether you're embarking on a short trip or an extended adventure, our Bolivia tours provide a perfect blend of cultural immersion and natural beauty. Let us help you craft the ideal package for your travels, making your trip to Lake Titicaca a highlight of your South American adventure.

The principal town on the shores of Lake Titicaca is Copacabana, a vibrant hub from which boats depart for the mystical Isla del Sol. This town is home to the impressive 16th-century Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana, dedicated to Bolivia's patron saint. Renowned across the country, Copacabana is celebrated for its rich cultural heritage, religious festivities, and traditional festivals that draw visitors year-round. Nestled between Mount Calvario and Mount Niño Calvario, this charming town is home to about 6,000 residents and offers a unique blend of spiritual significance and local tradition.

The name "Copacabana" is commonly believed to come from the Aymara phrase kota kahuana, which means "view of the lake." However, social scientist Mario Montaño Aragón uncovered an intriguing alternative in the "Archives of Indias" in Seville, Spain. He discovered that "Kotakawana" refers to an ancient Andean fertility deity, akin to the Greek goddess Aphrodite or the Roman Venus. This androgynous god is said to reside in Lake Titicaca, accompanied by mythical beings known as "Umantuus," akin to mermaids in Western lore, depicted in colonial sculptures.

Remarkably, the current Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana stands on the site of the ancient Temple of Kotakawana, a sacred place long before the Spanish arrival. Today, small fertility temples dedicated to Kotakawana can still be found along the shores of Lake Titicaca in Bolivia and Peru, underscoring the area’s profound spiritual significance that predates colonial history.

en.title: La Paz, the capital of Bolivia Tours  & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Bolivia  with Ada Tours
content_excerpts: La Paz, the capital of Bolivia Tours  & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Bolivia  with Ada Tours

La Paz, aptly called the city that touches the sky, truly lives up to its name. Perched at an impressive altitude of 3,660 meters (12,008 feet), it is the highest capital city in the world. Nestled within a natural bowl surrounded by the high-altitude plains, the city’s sprawling neighborhoods climb the surrounding hills, reaching elevations between 3,000 and 4,100 meters. Dominating the skyline is the majestic, snow-capped Illimani, a triple-peaked sentinel that watches over the city. Serving as both the administrative and departmental capital of Bolivia, La Paz boasted a population of 789,585 according to the 2001 census. When combined with the neighboring cities of El Alto and Viacha, it forms Bolivia's most populous urban area, with over 1.6 million residents.

La Paz stands as Bolivia’s cultural heart, brimming with vibrant marketplaces that are woven into the city's fabric, ensuring you encounter them wherever you wander. The city also boasts a rich tapestry of museums and historical landmarks. Key sites include the Cathedral of San Francisco, where the saint's remains are interred; the Metropolitan Cathedral, which houses the remains of Sucre; and the Quemado Palace, the seat of the executive branch.

You can also visit the Congress building, which occasionally opens its doors to the public, and stroll along Jaen Street, a preserved relic from the Spanish era, home to ten intriguing museums. Other notable attractions are the Valle de la Luna (Valley of the Moon) and the Muela del Diablo (Devil's Tooth), a striking geological formation ideal for hiking. Don’t miss the Cine-Teatro Municipal, a 19th-century gem, the Universidad Mayor de San Andrés, the largest state university in Bolivia, and the General Cemetery, the resting place of many Bolivian presidents. Explore the historic house of Simon Bolivar and take in the unique landscapes and cultural landmarks that make La Paz a city like no other.

The city is ideally situated close to a wealth of natural wonders and ancient ruins. Many visitors opt for day trips to the Tiahuanacu ruins, which, predating Machu Picchu by thousands of years, hold equal historical significance. The allure of Tiahuanacu is so strong that Chilean and Peruvian itineraries often feature this site, despite it being located in Bolivia. Another popular excursion is to Lake Titicaca and the lakeside town of Copacabana, renowned for its cathedral, which houses the revered Virgen de Copacabana, a significant deity of the lake.

content_excerpts: Tours to Copacabana & Lake Titicaca(Bolivia)   & Vacation packages | Guided trips to Bolivia  with Ada Tours

Embark on an unforgettable trip to Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, with one of our expertly crafted Bolivia tours. Whether you're seeking a guided tour to Lake Titicaca or planning to explore on your own, our travel packages are designed to showcase the best of this stunning region.

Choose a tour to Lake Titicaca that fits your interests, from exploring the floating islands of the Uros people to discovering the rich cultural heritage of the region. Our Bolivia travel packages offer a seamless experience, ensuring that your journey is both enriching and hassle-free.

Whether you're embarking on a short trip or an extended adventure, our Bolivia tours provide a perfect blend of cultural immersion and natural beauty. Let us help you craft the ideal package for your travels, making your trip to Lake Titicaca a highlight of your South American adventure.

The principal town on the shores of Lake Titicaca is Copacabana, a vibrant hub from which boats depart for the mystical Isla del Sol. This town is home to the impressive 16th-century Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana, dedicated to Bolivia's patron saint. Renowned across the country, Copacabana is celebrated for its rich cultural heritage, religious festivities, and traditional festivals that draw visitors year-round. Nestled between Mount Calvario and Mount Niño Calvario, this charming town is home to about 6,000 residents and offers a unique blend of spiritual significance and local tradition.

The name "Copacabana" is commonly believed to come from the Aymara phrase kota kahuana, which means "view of the lake." However, social scientist Mario Montaño Aragón uncovered an intriguing alternative in the "Archives of Indias" in Seville, Spain. He discovered that "Kotakawana" refers to an ancient Andean fertility deity, akin to the Greek goddess Aphrodite or the Roman Venus. This androgynous god is said to reside in Lake Titicaca, accompanied by mythical beings known as "Umantuus," akin to mermaids in Western lore, depicted in colonial sculptures.

Remarkably, the current Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana stands on the site of the ancient Temple of Kotakawana, a sacred place long before the Spanish arrival. Today, small fertility temples dedicated to Kotakawana can still be found along the shores of Lake Titicaca in Bolivia and Peru, underscoring the area’s profound spiritual significance that predates colonial history.
